lines.text: You probably do this twenty times a day: double-clicking your home screen and furiously swiping every app away to save battery.
Stop doing it right now. Swiping your apps closed does not save your battery — it actually drains it faster.
Most users believe background apps are running live, burning your CPU and sucking power in the background.
They are not. Modern operating systems freeze background apps in RAM, where they consume zero CPU cycles and practically zero wattage.
When you force-quit an app, you purge its memory. Reopening it forces the processor to reload all code from flash storage, causing a massive power spike.
Apple's head of software Craig Federighi was asked if quitting apps saves battery. His verified answer was just four words: 'No and No.'
Your phone is engineered to manage its own memory. Leave the apps in RAM — and let your battery breathe.
